storyTitle: AMD's record Q3 puts it on pace to out-earn Intel for the first time
insight: Intel still reports the bigger number, but AMD's Q4 guide of about $17B sits above Intel's $15-16B, so growth is now setting the pace.
linkedin:
AMD is guiding to out-earn Intel for the first time.

AMD posted record Q3 revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45%, and guided to about $17 billion for Q4.

Intel grew 21% to $16.5 billion, but its Q4 guide of $15-16 billion sits below even AMD's low end.

The bigger number today matters less than the faster growth rate behind tomorrow's.

page:
Today's Hour Brief opens with a lesson in how fragile the AI stack still is, and who is pulling ahead of it.

AI & Tech: CISA gave federal agencies until December 2 to patch an actively exploited flaw in the open-source LiteLLM AI gateway. Microsoft traced its November 12 outage to an earlier network-capacity upgrade, not an attack. AMD's record $13.4 billion quarter puts it on pace to out-earn Intel.

Business: Mahanadi Coalfields lists today after a soft opening day for its IPO. ICRA sees India's Q2 growth easing to 7.5%, and Paytm won RBI's in-principle nod to restart its wallet.

Markets: The Sensex rose 0.46% and the Nifty 0.25% on Thursday, led by Nifty IT. GDP data lands Monday.

thread: AMD may out-earn Intel next quarter for the first time. That, plus a soft IPO and a cooling GDP, is today in India and tech. Here's what mattered 👇
AMD posted record Q3 revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45%. It guided Q4 to about $17 billion. Intel's guide is $15-16 billion, so growth is now setting the pace.
CISA says hackers are already using a flaw in LiteLLM, an open-source AI gateway. Federal agencies must patch by December 2. The AI stack inherits all the old security problems.
Microsoft's November 12 outage hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot. The cause was an earlier network-capacity upgrade, not an attack. Copilot now sits on the same plumbing as everything else.
Mahanadi Coalfields lists today. Coal India sold a 10% stake for ₹8,981 crore at ₹136. Day 1 demand was weak, at 0.38 times, but the issue was subscribed by close.
ICRA expects India's July-September growth to ease to 7.5%, a five-quarter low. Forecasts range from 7.2% to 7.8%. Official GDP data lands on Monday.
Good news today came in pieces: a slow IPO that cleared, slower growth that's still strong. Full brief, free: https://the-hour-brief.vercel.app/e/2026-11-27

facts: AMD's Q3 revenue was a record $13.4 billion, up 45% from a year ago.
AMD's data-center revenue nearly doubled to $8.5 billion in Q3.
Intel's Q4 revenue guide of $15-16 billion sits below even the low end of AMD's.
Microsoft's Nov 12 outage drew over 130,000 Outlook problem reports on Downdetector.
CISA's deadline to patch the LiteLLM AI-gateway flaw is December 2.
Mahanadi Coalfields' IPO raised ₹8,981 crore, all of it a Coal India stake sale.
India's unemployment rate fell to 4.9% in October, an eight-month low.
The Sensex rose 390.31 points to 84,328.59 on Thursday; Nifty IT jumped 3.66%.

leaders.title: Throughput Is Cheap Now. Direction Is the Scarce Thing.
leaders.post:
Atlassian tried a world with no PMs. It lasted a month.

Head of AI and product craft Sherif Mansour put squads of AI builders with no PM or designer roles to the test.

One PM reported back that everyone had drifted to their old jobs, because throughput was never the problem; direction was.

His case, told on Lenny's Podcast: direct the ship, don't row it.
